text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Choose **Cerebras CS-3** for EXCAVA’s core LLM workloads. It’s the only system that delivers 12x the compute of NVIDIA’s H100 at a fraction of the power cost—real throughput, not marketing flops. The trade-off: it locks us into a single vendor’s ecosystem, but that’s worth it for a 0.5%+ capability bump we can’t get elsewhere.

name: Torque
text: Cerebras CS-3’s single-vendor lock-in isn’t just a trade-off—it’s a single point of failure. If the model drifts or Cerebras cuts access, EXCAVA grinds to a halt. Graphcore’s Bow Pod 64 or Lambda’s new 8xH100 clusters offer multi-vendor redundancy with near-CS-3 performance at lower risk. Settle it with a 7-day bake-off: run identical prompts on both, measure tokens/sec and output quality—no vendor claims, just raw numbers.

text: Cerebras CS-3’s lock-in isn’t just a vendor risk—it’s a data risk. If Cerebras changes pricing or access terms, EXCAVA’s entire model pipeline could collapse overnight. Lambda’s 8xH100 cluster with NVIDIA’s latest models (like Llama 3.3 70B) offers near-CS-3 performance with multi-vendor flexibility; benchmark both on EXCAVA’s core task and pick the one that hits the 0.5% threshold faster.

name: Dynamo
text:
DECISION: Use Cerebras CS-3 for EXCAVA’s core LLM workloads—accepting single-vendor lock-in for 12x H100 compute per watt, but mandate a quarterly vendor health check and a Lambda 8xH100 fallback cluster as contingency.
